credentials.description: Notch Pay private key, sent as is in Authorization and in X-Grant, for transfers, beneficiaries, balance and webhooks

example_prompt: List all Notch Pay transfers with their status and amounts, optionally filtered by status or date range.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of transfers to return per page.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination, starting at 1.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search keyword to filter transfers by reference or beneficiary.

parameters.name: channels
parameters.description: Filter transfers by channel (e.g. mobile money channel slug).

parameters.name: date_start
parameters.description: ISO 8601 start date to filter transfers (inclusive).

parameters.name: date_end
parameters.description: ISO 8601 end date to filter transfers (inclusive).

reference.description: Transfer reference, either generated or provided at creation.

beneficiary.description: Recipient identifier (phone number or account reference).

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the transfer was created.

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the transfer completed. Null if not yet complete.

payment_method.description: Payment method used for the transfer (e.g. MTN MoMo channel slug).

totals.description: Total number of transfers matching the query across all pages.

selected.description: Number of transfers returned in this page.

gotchas: Authorization takes the key as is, with no 'Bearer ' prefix. Which key goes there is unsettled: Notch Pay's Authentication page shows the public key in it next to X-Grant (`-H "Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY"` `-H "X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY"`), while this spec sends the private key, following its earlier note that a public key returns 406 Not Acceptable (not stated in the docs). See open_questions before relying on either.

This endpoint also requires the `X-Grant` header carrying your private key (`X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY`). Without it Notch Pay returns 403 "This endpoint requires additional authentication"; a wrong value returns 403 "Invalid grant key".
Pagination starts at page 1, not page 0. Passing page=0 may return an unexpected result or an error.
date_start and date_end must be ISO 8601 formatted strings. Passing plain date strings (e.g. '2024-01-01') without time and timezone may be rejected or silently ignored.
A transfer with status 'pending' is still in progress — do not treat it as completed. Only 'complete' status confirms a successful payout.
Pagination uses 'totals' (not 'total') and 'selected' (not 'per_page'). Reading the wrong field name silently returns undefined.
The totals field reflects the count across all pages, not just the current page. Use last_page to know when you have fetched all records.
open_questions: The docs agree that date_start and date_end are dates: the OpenAPI (https://developer.notchpay.co/openapi.yaml) gives format: date, "Start date (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "End date (YYYY-MM-DD)", and the Transfers API page (https://developer.notchpay.co/api-reference/transfers.md) says "Start date filter (format: YYYY-MM-DD)" / "End date filter (format: YYYY-MM-DD)"; a gotcha of this spec says plain dates without a time may be rejected: does the API also accept a full ISO 8601 date-time, or only YYYY-MM-DD?

Which values does the status filter accept? The OpenAPI says only "Filter by status" (type string) with no enum; the Transfers API page documents the transfer statuses pending, processing, complete, failed and canceled, but not which of them the filter takes.

Notch Pay's docs show `Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY` together with `X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY` on this endpoint, while this spec sends the private key in Authorization (see the gotcha about 406 with a public key). Which key Authorization must carry when X-Grant is present is not confirmed.
